subject: german
title: Numbers, Days & Colours: The Foundations
welcome_lead: Build your German core vocab — numbers 1 to 20, days of the week, and colours that pop up everywhere in GCSE listening.
meta_desc: GCSE German vocab foundations: numbers, days, months and colours with quick-fire practice.
final_note: Solid start! These words anchor every other topic — dates, times, descriptions, all built on this base.

concepts.def: One, two, three — the start of counting 1 to 20.
Monday — first weekday; days start with capitals in German.
January — months are also capitalised in German.
Red — colour adjective, no capital letter.
Black — note the 'sch' sound and ending -z.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The first ten are: eins, zwei, drei, vier, fünf, sechs, sieben, acht, neun, zehn.

From 13 to 19, you add -zehn to the digit: dreizehn, vierzehn, fünfzehn. Watch out for sechzehn (no -s) and siebzehn (no -en).

Twenty is zwanzig.

In order: Montag, Dienstag, Mittwoch, Donnerstag, Freitag, Samstag, Sonntag.

Mittwoch literally means 'mid-week'. Some regions say Sonnabend instead of Samstag.

Use am + day: am Montag = on Monday.

Learn: rot (red), blau (blue), gelb (yellow), grün (green), weiß (white), schwarz (black), braun (brown), orange.

As standalone adjectives (after ist) they don't change: Das Auto ist rot.
